subject: computer-science

items.q: What does a binary search need to work?
items.misconception: It works on any unsorted list.
items.random_wrong: It only works on numbers, never words.
items.why: Binary search repeatedly halves a SORTED list; linear search works on any order but is slower on large data.

items.q: Must an algorithm be written in code?
items.correct: No — it's a step-by-step method (e.g. pseudocode or a flowchart).
items.misconception: Yes, an algorithm has to be program code.
items.random_wrong: Pseudocode runs directly on a computer.
items.why: An algorithm is the logic; it can be expressed many ways and later coded.

items.q: Which is generally faster on a large sorted list?
items.why: Binary search discards half the data each step, so it scales far better than checking items one by one.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Computer Science (1CP2) specification; Problem Solving With Programming
